Typografische Monatsblätter covers, 1972–1973

Wolfgang Weingart’s series of covers for the Swiss trade journal TM, which break its grid with stepped blocks, spaced-out letters, and heavy bars.

Source
Letterform Archive: Legacies of Swiss Style, Part 2—Wolfgang Weingart
Creator
Wolfgang Weingart
Made
1972–1973 (Letterform Archive)
Style
New Wave typography (agent-proposed, not yet reviewed by a person)
Moods
Kinetic, rebellious, layered, experimental, didactic
Evidence
Inspected Letterform Archive’s photographs of seven covers held by the Archive (Nr. 1, 5, and 12 of 1972; Nr. 2, 3, 6.7, and 10 of 1973), 1996 to 2965 px wide, in scratchpad copies. Not stored.
Reviewed
28 September 2026
Rights
Link and metadata only. License: unverified. Rights policy

Context

The TM editorial board asked Weingart, a new board member, to design fifteen covers for the 1972 and 1973 print runs. The covers are set in Akzidenz-Grotesk and have “a conspicuous variety of line weights, imbalanced asymmetries, and stepped text blocks intersected by bold rectilinear shapes”. Letterform Archive.

Jan Tschichold wrote to the editor that he hoped this was the last issue with a Weingart cover, and later called Weingart “the anti-typographer”. Letterform Archive.

The cover of Nr. 6.7/1973 carries the name of April Greiman, Weingart’s student; see her later work.

Observed

  • Nr. 2/1973: a quotation in small capitals with very wide gaps between the letters fills four lines; below it, “NACHRICHT” in heavy capitals runs up in an arc, each letter rotated.
  • Nr. 1/1972: “Typographie realisiert Sprache” in large black grotesque is cut into cells by thin vertical rules; a narrow text column at right ends each line with a black rectangle of a different length.
  • Nr. 5/1972: “SPRACHE:” in heavy condensed capitals, then lines in a regular grotesque, each underlined by a grey bar. Weight changes inside one line (“Darstellungs-zeichen.”), and the last word “Gebärden.” is letterspaced.
  • Nr. 12/1972 and Nr. 3/1973: grey or white panels with stepped edges overlap the text blocks, and a justified line opens into very large word gaps.
  • Nr. 6.7/1973: “A P R I L G R E I M A N” and “F E E L I N G T Y P O G R A P H Y” in thin capitals with very wide letterspacing, around a centered photograph.
  • Nr. 10/1973: large heavy type in mixed sizes, a black arrow bar, black dots, a triangle, and small rotated text on a thin angled line.
  • Each cover keeps the same footer, the three journal names with bold initials, and a number at the top.

Why it belongs

The series is a catalogue of the style’s type moves inside one fixed frame: wide tracking, rotation, stepping, weight changes, and bars. The fixed footer and number show that the disorder is controlled.

The palette is almost only black, grey, and paper, so colour is not needed for the style.

Borrow

Keep a fixed header and footer, and change only the middle composition from issue to issue.

Set a quotation in small capitals with gaps of one or two letter widths between the letters.

End lines of a narrow column with black bars of different lengths instead of a clean rag.
